title: Customer-probe replay harness for throughput certification and autoscaling validation
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Build a customer-probe replay harness (CPR) that lets us certify Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees and validate autoscaling policies against real customer traffic shapes without exposing PII. The CPR will accept sanitized request traces (event-time preserved), apply deterministic latency and error modeling, and drive fleet-level scenarios (steady-state, step-load, sawtooth, spike-with-cooldown) while measuring tail latency, throughput, and cost metrics. The goal is a repeatable, auditable acceptance test that product and SRE can run before signing off on capacity-related SLAs and autoscaler rules.
implementation_plan:
1) Define trace ingestion format (event_time, route, model_variant, token_counts, intent_label, anonymized_customer_id).
2) Build trace sanitizer with k-anonymity sampling and redaction rules. Integrate optional token hashing for debug correlation.
3) Implement replay driver (shadow-agent) that can run in: a) client-side synthetic mode, b) in-cluster pod mode to avoid external network noise.
4) Add injectors: latency distribution overlay, model-failure injector (5xx/429 mix), and KV-cache-miss simulator.
5) Orchestrator: scenario DSL to define cluster size, scaling rules, and parallelism. Persist runs to S3 and tag with run metadata.
6) Metrics and postprocessing: compute p50/p95/p99 latency per route, per-model throughput, per-token cost estimate, and autoscaler decision timeline.
7) Integrate with Console: create a run summary view and linkable run artifacts for customer acceptance.
8) Security review and privacy attestation with legal for customer-trace usage.
acceptance_criteria:
1) CPR can ingest and sanitize a 24-hour customer trace (1M requests) and produce an event-time preserving replay plan within 30 minutes.
2) Driver can run the five canonical scenarios against a 50-node Dedicated pool and produce stable p99 estimates within ±5% on repeat runs.
3) Autoscaling policy validation: for each defined policy, CPR demonstrates correct scale-up/scale-down decisions on synthetic step-up and spike scenarios; recorded decision timelines must match expected thresholds in spec.
4) Privacy: all runs using customer traces must pass the sanitizer audit checklist; no raw PII is written to logs or S3.
5) Console integration: run artifacts link to a human-readable summary and raw metrics CSV; SRE/PM can reproduce results via a single CLI command.
test_matrix: Workload shapes: steady (λ constant), linear ramp, step-up 10x, sawtooth 10min period, random burst (Poisson with heavy tail)
Model variants: base_fp16, q4_0, q4_1 (to validate kernel selection and quantization effects)
KV cache states: warm-cache (80% hit), cold-cache (5% hit), mixed
Network conditions: nominal, +25ms tail latency overlay, +100ms overlay
notes: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/cpr-design (contains DSL spec and sanitizer rules)
Related ticket: ENG-4721 (dedicated-capacity-load-harness) — CPR reuses the replay format but adds event-time preservation and privacy controls
SRE asked for per-node tail breakdown — included in metrics plan above
